title: BIF semantic fidelity — `lists` key ops coerce where OTP compares exactly, `maps` BIFs raise badarg where OTP raises `{badmap, Map}`, and `ExecError` `Display` invents an atom table that cannot resolve real MFAs
blocked_by: RF-004 (atom-index serialization: RF-004 R2 mints Atom::TRY_CLAUSE at index 77; RF-007 R3 mints Atom::BADMAP and MUST take the next free index after RF-004 lands — whoever lands second re-pins, and this ordering makes that deterministically RF-007; both alignment tests still required)
purpose:
Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` (reviewed at `fd71c5e`, 2026-07-23; 11 parallel subsystem reviewers, each finding adversarially re-verified by an independent refuter), MEDIUM cluster, findings M2, M3, M6. Evidence pin for THIS brief: beamr main `a0359a2`. RE-PIN: all three files (`native/stdlib_stubs/lists_bifs.rs`, `native/stdlib_stubs/maps_bifs.rs`, `error.rs`) are BYTE-IDENTICAL between `fd71c5e` and `a0359a2` — every cited line number holds verbatim at the current head. This is one mechanical lane: three narrow, independently-testable fidelity gaps in code that answers questions Erlang programs ask constantly. None is a memory-safety bug; all three are the VM confidently returning the wrong answer.

M2 — `lists` key operations use `==` (numeric coercion) where OTP specifies `=:=` (exact equality). Review verbatim: "`lists:member(1, [1.0])` returns `true` (OTP: `false`); key ops match/replace/delete the wrong tuple across int/float." `crates/beamr/src/native/stdlib_stubs/lists_bifs.rs`, FOUR sites, re-pinned at `a0359a2`:
  * `:82` in `bif_lists_member` (`:76`) — `compare::numeric_eq(*element, *candidate)` (the review's `:81` is the enclosing `elements.iter().any(|candidate| {` line)
  * `:94` in `bif_lists_keyfind` (`:86`)
  * `:257` in `bif_lists_keystore` (`:245`)
  * `:298` in `bif_lists_keydelete` (`:289`)
Exactly the four BIFs the review names, and no others in the file. The correct helper already exists and is one identifier away: `crate::term::compare::exact_eq(left, right)` (`crates/beamr/src/term/compare/mod.rs:17-21`), implementing `=:=` via `exact_cmp`/`compare_exact` (`:25-26`, `:198-222`) — the module's own header line reads "Term ordering and equality — `==` (number coercion) and `=:=` (exact)." The dangerous part of this fix is what it must NOT touch: `numeric_eq` (`compare/mod.rs:34`) has four other production call sites where `==` is CORRECT and changing them would be a regression — `interpreter/opcodes/guards.rs:85-86` (the `==`/`/=` comparison opcodes), `native/bifs.rs:154-162` (the `==`/`/=` BIFs, registered at `:33`), and `ets/match_spec.rs:335-336` (match-spec `CompareOp::Eq`/`Ne`). This is a targeted four-site change, not a sweep of `numeric_eq`.

M3 — `maps` BIFs raise `badarg` where OTP raises `{badmap, Map}`. Review verbatim: "no `badmap` atom exists in the crate; error-handling that distinguishes `badmap` silently mis-branches." `crates/beamr/src/native/stdlib_stubs/maps_bifs.rs:537` (re-pinned, unmoved) is `map_entries`: `let map = Map::new(term).ok_or_else(badarg)?;` — and it is the pattern, not the only instance. Sibling not-a-map guards in the same file at `:160` (`bif_maps_find`), `:169`, `:179` (`bif_maps_keys`), `:190` (`bif_maps_values`), and more; `badarg()` at `:607` returns the bare `Term::atom(Atom::BADARG)`. The atom confirms the review: `crates/beamr/src/atom/table.rs:14-90` runs `OK(0)` .. `INFINITY(76)` with NO `BADMAP`, and `COMMON_ATOMS` (`:101-179`) has no `("badmap", ...)` row. The DESIGN CONSTRAINT that makes this more than a rename: `{badmap, Map}` is a 2-TUPLE and must be allocated on the process heap, but `map_entries(term: Term)` has no `ProcessContext` — so either the context is threaded to the guard sites, or the badmap Term is minted where a context IS in hand. THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, complete with its GC dance: `native/gate3_bifs/type_conversion.rs:325-343` mints `{badkey, Key}` by parking the key in `x0`, calling `context.ensure_heap_space(3)`, re-reading `x0`, then `context.alloc_tuple_prereserved(&[Term::atom(Atom::BADKEY), key])`. `Atom::BADKEY` (`table.rs:38`, row `:126`) shows the mint shape; `badkey_prereserved` (`type_conversion.rs:340-343`) shows the allocation shape; `bif_maps_find` (`maps_bifs.rs:155-173`) shows the `context.with_rooted(...)` + `ensure_heap_space` + `rooted(...)` re-read pattern the same file already uses. Nothing here is invented.

M6 — `ExecError` `Display` builds a FRESH atom table on every format and therefore cannot resolve any runtime atom. Review verbatim: "`error.rs:203` — the `Display` impls for `Undef`/`Badfun`/`Badarity`/`GuardBifUnavailable` build a fresh `AtomTable::with_common_atoms()` (only ~79 built-ins), so `format!(\"{err}\")` on a real MFA prints `undefined function #<unknown atom>:#<unknown atom>/1`. Actively misleading; the real data only appears via `format_with_atoms`." Re-pinned at `a0359a2`, FOUR construction sites in the `Display` impl (`error.rs:193-283`): `:203` (`Undef`), `:215` (`Badfun`), `:223` (`Badarity`), `:268` (`GuardBifUnavailable`). Module and function atoms of any user-loaded module are interned at runtime with indices at or above `COMMON_ATOMS.len()`, so `fallback.resolve(...)` returns `None` and the format falls to `"#<unknown atom>"` (`:207-208`, `:272-273`). Two costs, not one: the output is undiagnosable, AND every `Display` call allocates a `DashMap` and inserts 77 `String`s to learn nothing. This finding is directly load-bearing on EMB-001, which shipped `GuardBifUnavailable` precisely to make a refusal diagnosable and whose 2026-07-18 pre-review amendment RULED that "plain `Display` resolves through a fresh common-atoms table and renders the fallback token for runtime atoms" with `format_with_atoms` as the exact-string carrier. M6 says the fallback token itself is the problem: `#<unknown atom>` discards the ONE piece of information `Display` actually holds — the atom INDEX — and reads to a user as if the atom were corrupt rather than merely unresolvable without a table. Note also the pre-existing `_ => self.to_string()` catch-all at `error.rs:328` in `format_with_atoms` (already flagged in EMB-001's D3): every variant not explicitly handled there inherits `Display`'s output, so fixing `Display` honestly improves the atom-table-carrying path too.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided, one carved fork OQ-A): three mechanical fidelity fixes, one lane, one red-first commit each. OTP-29 IS THE REFERENCE SEMANTICS for M2 and M3 and every claim is measured against it by hand — the standard set by `0a1f6ed`, whose lesson was that a beamr test asserting beamr's current shape is evidence of nothing. No new wake paths, no timers, no configuration.

D1 M2 — FOUR SITES, `numeric_eq` -> `exact_eq`. `lists_bifs.rs:82`, `:94`, `:257`, `:298` change to `compare::exact_eq(...)`. NOTHING ELSE CHANGES. The four OTHER production `numeric_eq` call sites — `guards.rs:85-86`, `bifs.rs:154-162`, `match_spec.rs:335-336` — are CORRECT `==` semantics and touching them is a STOP. `bif_lists_keysort` (`lists_bifs.rs:270`) uses `compare::cmp` for ORDERING, which is standard-order and correctly coercing; it is not in scope. `bif_lists_sort` likewise. The drafter reads OTP-29's `lists` documentation for each of the four (member/keyfind/keystore/keydelete) and confirms `=:=` is specified for each individually rather than generalizing from `member/2`.

D2 M3 — MINT `badmap`, RAISE `{badmap, Map}`. (i) Atom: append `pub const BADMAP: Self = Self(77);` after `INFINITY = Self(76)` (`atom/table.rs:90`) with the matching `("badmap", Atom::BADMAP)` row appended at the END of `COMMON_ATOMS` (`:178`). INDEX AND ROW POSITION MUST MATCH: `with_common_atoms` (`:205-217`) inserts by `atom.index()` then stores `next_index = COMMON_ATOMS.len()`, so a misaligned const silently corrupts every subsequent `intern`. COORDINATION NOTE: RF-004 R2 also appends an atom (`TRY_CLAUSE`). If both land, the second to land takes index 78 and adjusts — whoever lands second re-pins; a merge that gives two constants the same index is a STOP and the R2 alignment test below catches it. (ii) Reason: `{badmap, Map}` is a 2-tuple carrying the offending term, minted via the `badkey_prereserved` shape (`type_conversion.rs:340-343`) with the GC dance that precedent already performs — park the term, `ensure_heap_space(3)`, re-read, `alloc_tuple_prereserved`. `bif_maps_find`'s `context.with_rooted(&[...], |context, roots| { context.ensure_heap_space(3)?; let x = context.rooted(roots, 0)?; ... })` (`maps_bifs.rs:165-172`) is the in-file idiom for rooting across the reserve. (iii) Plumbing: `map_entries(term: Term)` (`:536`) has no `ProcessContext`. Thread the context to it and to the sibling guard sites, OR mint the badmap at the outer BIF where a context is in hand. Drafter's call, stated with reasons — but the CHOICE MUST BE UNIFORM across the file, not per-site. (iv) SCOPE: every not-a-map guard in `maps_bifs.rs` — `:160`, `:169`, `:179`, `:190`, `:537`, and any the drafter's own enumeration finds — is classified: BADMAP (the argument was supposed to be a map) or genuinely BADARG (something else was wrong, e.g. arity, a non-closure, a bad iterator). `ok_or_else(badarg)` sites that guard `map.key(index)`/`map.value(index)` INSIDE a valid map (`:181`, `:192`, `:541-542`) are internal-invariant failures, NOT badmap — do not blanket-rename.

D3 M6 — `Display` STOPS PRETENDING IT HAS AN ATOM TABLE (recommended; the fork is OQ-A). Replace the four `AtomTable::with_common_atoms()` constructions (`error.rs:203`, `:215`, `:223`, `:268`) with an allocation-free resolution of the COMMON atoms only, and render any unresolvable atom as its INDEX in a form that cannot be mistaken for a name — e.g. `#<atom 1042>` in place of `#<unknown atom>`. Two properties bought: (a) HONESTY — the output no longer implies the atom is unknown to the VM when it is merely unknown to this formatter, and the index is a real handle a reader can resolve against a live table; (b) the per-format `DashMap` + 77 `String` allocations disappear from an error path. Mechanism: a `pub(crate) fn resolve_common(atom: Atom) -> Option<&'static str>` in `atom/table.rs` doing a linear scan of the existing `COMMON_ATOMS` const slice (77 entries, no allocation), reused by all four sites and by `term::format`'s `#<unknown atom>` sites (`term/format.rs:52`, `:157`) if the drafter finds the same misleading rendering there. `format_with_atoms` (`error.rs:288-328`) REMAINS the exact-name carrier and is unchanged in behavior — but note its `_ => self.to_string()` catch-all at `:328`, so this change improves that path too, and EMB-001's D4 wall pins the GuardBifUnavailable strings in BOTH channels and must be re-pinned in the same commit to the new fallback form. RELATIONSHIP TO EMB-001: this REFINES the 2026-07-18 amendment (which ruled the fallback token acceptable), it does not overturn the ruling that `format_with_atoms` is the exact-string carrier. The tear should be told this explicitly.

D4 RED FIRST, per finding (R1). M2: a test asserting `lists:member(1, [1.0])` is `false` and that keyfind/keystore/keydelete do not match/replace/delete across the int/float boundary — currently RED on all four. M3: a test asserting the not-a-map error reason is the 2-tuple `{badmap, NotAMap}` carrying the offending term — currently RED (bare `badarg`). M6: a test asserting `format!("{err}")` on an `Undef` carrying RUNTIME-interned atoms renders resolvable output — currently RED (`#<unknown atom>:#<unknown atom>`). Loaded-bytecode coverage where the semantics are user-observable: M2 and M3 are BIF-level and testable at the BIF boundary, but at least one loaded-bytecode leg per finding (real-erlc fixture, `if_probe`/`fc_probe` harness shape, `erlc` at `/opt/homebrew/bin/erlc`) proves the semantics as a program sees them — a Rust-side assertion alone does not prove an Erlang program observes the fix.

D5 SCOPE FENCE. M1 (binary-match bignum), H1, H2 are RF-004. M12 is RF-005. C1/C2/H3/H4/H5/H6/M7/M9 are other lanes. M4 (distribution big-int decoder) and M5 (validator frame size) are NOT in this brief. If the M3 classification surfaces a maps BIF whose defect is something other than the badmap reason, it is recorded and deferred, not fixed opportunistically.

OQ-A (carved for the tear): D3's stance — `Display` renders `#<atom N>` and never constructs a table — versus the alternative of giving `Display` real resolution by routing it through a process-wide or thread-local atom table. Recommendation: D3 as written. The alternative reintroduces ambient global state into an error path, is at odds with the crate's explicit design that atoms are opaque outside `beamr` and compared by value (`atom/table.rs:6-11`), and would make `Display`'s output depend on which table happened to be installed — a worse kind of misleading than the one being fixed. But the alternative DOES deliver the review's literal ask (real MFAs in `Display`), so the tear should rule.

requirements.title: RED — three failing fidelity tests at current bytes, each with its OTP-29 differential recorded
requirements.spec: Per D4: (i) M2 — `lists:member(1, [1.0])` is `false`; `lists:keyfind(1, 1, [{1.0, x}])` is `false`; `keystore`/`keydelete` do not act across int/float. (ii) M3 — a `maps` BIF called with a non-map argument yields reason `{badmap, NotAMap}` carrying the offending term. (iii) M6 — `format!("{err}")` on an `ExecError::Undef` whose module/function atoms were interned at RUNTIME renders resolvable output rather than `#<unknown atom>`. Each finding also gets at least one loaded-bytecode leg via a beamr-authored real-erlc fixture, so the semantics are proven as an Erlang program observes them.
acceptance: All three tests exist, compile, and FAIL at `a0359a2` with the exact wrong behavior transcribed into the failure message; the RED transcript is in the commit body

The OTP-29 differential for M2 (all four BIFs, individually) and M3 is run by hand and its verbatim output recorded — the reference-semantics claim is measured, not asserted, per the `0a1f6ed` standard
Each `.erl` fixture is beamr-authored and compiled by the box's real OTP-29 `erlc`; both `.erl` and `.beam` committed; no other project's artifact bytes used
M2's test covers BOTH directions per BIF: the coercing match that must STOP matching, and an exact match that must KEEP matching — a fix that breaks exact equality must go red

requirements.title: M2 — the four `lists` key operations compare with `=:=`
requirements.spec: Per D1: `lists_bifs.rs:82` (`bif_lists_member`), `:94` (`bif_lists_keyfind`), `:257` (`bif_lists_keystore`), `:298` (`bif_lists_keydelete`) call `compare::exact_eq` instead of `compare::numeric_eq`. No other call site of `numeric_eq` changes.
acceptance: R1(i) goes GREEN across all four BIFs, matching the recorded OTP-29 differential

`compare::numeric_eq` is UNCHANGED at `guards.rs:85-86`, `bifs.rs:154-162`, and `match_spec.rs:335-336` — verified by grep and by the existing `==`/`/=` tests staying green. `==` must still coerce (`1 == 1.0` remains `true`); a fix that makes `==` exact is a STOP
`bif_lists_sort`/`bif_lists_keysort` (`:270`) still use standard-order `compare::cmp` — ORDERING is not equality and is out of scope
OTP-29 semantics confirmed per BIF individually, not generalized from `member/2`; the four confirmations are in the handoff

requirements.title: M3 — mint `badmap` and raise `{badmap, Map}` from the not-a-map guards
requirements.spec: Per D2: `Atom::BADMAP` appended to `atom/table.rs` with its `COMMON_ATOMS` row at the SAME position index; the not-a-map guards in `maps_bifs.rs` (`:160`, `:169`, `:179`, `:190`, `:537`, plus the drafter's own enumeration) return the 2-tuple `{badmap, Term}` built via the `badkey_prereserved` shape (`type_conversion.rs:340-343`) with the rooted-reserve dance `bif_maps_find` (`:165-172`) already uses. Internal-invariant guards inside a VALID map (`:181`, `:192`, `:541-542`) stay `badarg`.
acceptance: R1(ii) goes GREEN: a non-map argument yields `{badmap, NotAMap}` with the offending term intact, matching the recorded OTP-29 differential

Atom index and `COMMON_ATOMS` row position are aligned — a test asserts `with_common_atoms().resolve(Atom::BADMAP) == Some("badmap")` AND `with_common_atoms().len() == COMMON_ATOMS.len()`, so a misaligned mint is caught at the table rather than as a mis-resolved error string. This test also catches an RF-004/RF-007 index collision if both lanes land

EVERY not-a-map guard in `maps_bifs.rs` is enumerated and classified BADMAP or BADARG with a stated reason; the classification is uniform (one plumbing choice for the whole file, per D2(iii)), and the enumeration is in the commit body

NO STALE TERM ACROSS THE RESERVE: the offending term is rooted across `ensure_heap_space` and re-read after, per the `bif_maps_find` idiom — introducing an H3/H4/H5-class instance while fixing M3 is a STOP
Internal-invariant guards inside a valid map are NOT renamed to badmap; a blanket rename must go red

requirements.title: M6 — `Display` renders the atom index instead of constructing a table that cannot resolve it
requirements.spec: Per D3 (subject to the OQ-A ruling): a `pub(crate) fn resolve_common(atom: Atom) -> Option<&'static str>` in `atom/table.rs` scanning the existing `COMMON_ATOMS` const slice with no allocation, used at all four `Display` sites (`error.rs:203`, `:215`, `:223`, `:268`) in place of `AtomTable::with_common_atoms()`; unresolvable atoms render as their index in a form that cannot be read as a name. `format_with_atoms` (`:288-328`) remains the exact-name carrier.
acceptance: R1(iii) goes GREEN: `format!("{err}")` on an `Undef` with runtime-interned atoms yields output carrying the atom INDICES and never the misleading `#<unknown atom>` for a valid-but-uncommon atom
`AtomTable::with_common_atoms()` is no longer constructed anywhere in `error.rs`'s `Display` impl (grep); the error path allocates no `DashMap` and no `String`s to format
Common atoms still resolve to their names — a `Display` of an error carrying `Atom::BADARG` still prints `badarg`; the change is strictly about the unresolvable case

EMB-001's D4 wall (`crates/beamr/tests/guard_bif_unavailable.rs`) — which pins the `GuardBifUnavailable` strings byte-exact in BOTH the `format_with_atoms` and plain-`Display` channels — is re-pinned to the new fallback form IN THIS COMMIT. Leaving that wall red, or weakening it to stop asserting the plain-Display shape, is a STOP
`format_with_atoms`'s behavior is unchanged for every variant it handles explicitly; the pre-existing `_ => self.to_string()` catch-all at `:328` is NOT widened and no new `_ =>` is introduced
`term/format.rs:52` and `:157` are inspected for the same misleading rendering; either fixed with the shared helper or explicitly excluded with a reason in the handoff

requirements.title: Permanent walls — the three fidelity claims cannot silently regress
requirements.spec: The R1 tests become permanent release-gated walls, plus a differential-fidelity note at each fixed site naming OTP as the reference. For M2, a wall that pins BOTH the exact-equality behavior of the four `lists` BIFs AND the coercing behavior of `==`/`/=` — the two must never be conflated again.
acceptance: All walls run under `cargo test --workspace` (the gates.json `tests` leg) and pass ten consecutive isolated runs each

Fail-first recorded and reverted, per fix independently: revert R2 -> the M2 wall goes red on `member(1, [1.0])`; revert R3 -> the M3 wall goes red at the reason shape; revert R4 -> the M6 wall goes red at the rendered output. Each RED transcript is in the landing commit body
The M2 wall asserts the `==`/`/=` coercing half alongside the `=:=` exact half, so a future 'simplification' that unifies them goes red

Each fixed site carries a one-line comment naming OTP as the reference semantics and what the pre-fix behavior was — the `func_info`/`if_end` documentation habit the review praised ("the recent `func_info`/`if_end` fixes are correct and documented inline")

boundaries: `==` MUST STILL COERCE. `compare::numeric_eq` and its call sites at `guards.rs:85-86`, `bifs.rs:154-162`, `match_spec.rs:335-336` are CORRECT and untouched. Only the four `lists_bifs.rs` sites change. A change that makes `==` exact is a STOP.
ORDERING IS NOT EQUALITY. `compare::cmp` / standard-order sorting (`bif_lists_sort`, `bif_lists_keysort`) is out of scope entirely.

OTP-29 IS THE REFERENCE. Every fidelity claim (exact-vs-coercing per BIF, badmap reason SHAPE) is measured against OTP-29 by hand and the output recorded, never inferred from beamr's own prior behavior — `0a1f6ed`'s self-consistent-but-wrong pin is the standing lesson.

ATOM INDEX AND ROW POSITION MUST MATCH. `with_common_atoms` inserts by `atom.index()` and sets `next_index = COMMON_ATOMS.len()`; a const whose index differs from its row position corrupts every subsequent `intern`. RF-004 R2 also appends an atom — whoever lands second re-pins, and the alignment test in R3 must catch a collision.

NO STALE TERM ACROSS THE RESERVE. R3 allocates a tuple on the process heap; the offending term must be rooted across `ensure_heap_space` and re-read after, per the in-file `bif_maps_find` idiom. Introducing an H3/H4/H5-class instance while fixing M3 is a STOP.

`format_with_atoms` STAYS THE EXACT-NAME CARRIER. R4 refines EMB-001's 2026-07-18 fallback-token amendment; it does not overturn the ruling that `format_with_atoms` carries exact strings. EMB-001's D4 wall is re-pinned in the same commit, never weakened.

ZERO new `#[allow]` of any kind; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` catch-all arms introduced to dodge an exhaustive match — the new `Atom::BADMAP` and any widened match must be handled honestly, and the pre-existing `error.rs:328` catch-all is not widened.
NO-POLLING: no new wake paths, no timers, no sleep/retry loops.
NO NEW CONFIG KNOBS — no configurable equality mode, no error-verbosity setting. Error formatting is not tunable.

BOTH wasm32 CLOSURES STAY GREEN. `error.rs`, `atom/table.rs`, and the stdlib-stub BIFs are shared code compiled for the threaded AND the cooperative closure; `cargo check -p beamr-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked` and the wasm-tests leg must be green at the final head. No `ExecError` variant is added or removed by this brief — if that changes, `crates/beamr-wasm/src/reasons.rs` moves in the SAME commit with an additive row and the WPORT-5 coverage wall extends.

SCOPE FENCE: M1/H1/H2 (RF-004), M12 (RF-005), C1/C2/H3-H6/M4/M5/M7/M9 (other lanes) are NOT touched. A defect surfaced by the M3 classification that is not the badmap reason is recorded and deferred, not fixed opportunistically.
